D021-D013_h001.question_both:
I’ve just turned 42 this year, and between managing the night shift at the factory and being home to my wife, things have felt… off for a few months now. I don’t know when exactly it started, but I’ve been watching what I eat pretty closely. I used to grab fries or a burger with the crew after shift, but now I can’t stand the thought—like, if I eat something fatty, I feel like I’ll just balloon up overnight. So I stick to salads, plain chicken, black coffee. I’m down near 150 now, which is pretty light for my frame, and I *know* I keep losing, but I don’t feel like stopping.

I’m not *trying* to be thin, exactly—but the idea of gaining weight scares me. Not like a panic attack or anything, just this constant hum in the back of my head. Honestly, most days I just don’t feel like eating at all. Food doesn’t interest me. I’ve lost the spark at work too—hard to focus, easy to get irritated. I love my wife, but I’ve been keeping to myself. I can’t say if it’s the mood driving the eating changes… or the other way around. I just know I don’t feel like myself.
D021-D013_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been someone who prides myself on control—running a shift on the factory floor, keeping things on schedule, making sure everyone does their part. But lately, the control’s kind of… shifted. I watch what I eat all the time—down to the calorie. I’m at about 800 a day now, mostly plain rice, steamed vegetables, black coffee. I know it’s low, but if I eat more, or anything with fat or sugar, I just… panic. Like, one slice of pizza and I’ll balloon up overnight. It’s not rational, I get that, but the fear is overwhelming.

Over the past six months, I’ve lost nearly 40 pounds. My wife keeps asking if I’m sick, if I’m unhappy—she’s worried, says I’m withdrawn, not sleeping well, not interested in doing much outside work. And yeah, I’ve felt down. But it’s not like the sadness comes first. It’s the food, the weight, the fear—that’s what’s always on my mind. Even now, at this weight, I look in the mirror and see someone who needs to lose more. Gaining even a little feels like failure.
D021-D013_h001.question_b:
I’ve just turned 42, and lately, everything feels heavy—way heavier than the stress of managing shifts and safety checks at the factory. I used to take pride in providing for my wife and kids, but now I can’t even bring myself to eat with them. Most days, I skip lunch or just have black coffee. I don’t know… I just don’t feel hungry, and cooking feels like too much effort. My wife keeps saying I’m wasting away, and I guess she’s right—I’ve lost about 18 pounds in the past three months.

It’s not that I’m afraid of gaining weight or anything like that. In fact, I wouldn’t mind putting some weight back on—I feel weak. But food just doesn’t matter anymore. I used to enjoy a good meal, even desserts, and I don’t feel repulsed by high-calorie foods or scared they’ll make me fat. I just… don’t want them. I wake up tired, go through the motions at work, come home, and lie on the couch. I haven’t laughed in weeks. Even small things feel overwhelming, and I keep thinking I’m failing everyone.

I don’t know when it started, but I just stopped being hungry—actually, the thought of eating makes me anxious. I only eat a few bites now, usually just plain rice or lettuce, nothing with fat. I’ve lost a lot of weight, and people keep asking if I’m okay, but I actually feel *better* this way—lighter, more in control.

The scale is my first check every morning. If it goes up even a little, I feel like a failure—like I’ve done something wrong. I know I’m thin, but I can’t stop. Gaining even a pound terrifies me. It’s not just about looks; it’s like, if I gain weight, I’m weak. Like I’ve lost discipline. 

I do feel sad sometimes—exhausted, numb—but it’s not constant. The thing I focus on most is my body. I measure everything, count every calorie. I know I’m losing weight fast, but stopping feels more dangerous than continuing. I just can’t risk gaining it back.
D021-D013_h015.question_b: I’ve been working as a content moderator for about a year now, and it’s been really hard on me. I spend all day looking at violent, disturbing stuff, and honestly, I don’t know how to process any of it anymore. For the past three months, I just haven’t felt like myself. I don’t enjoy anything—not scrolling, not going out, not even texting my friends. I feel heavy, tired all the time, and honestly, I’ve stopped caring about a lot of things, including food. I used to eat full meals, but now I just pick at things—maybe a few bites at dinner, if that. I’ve lost weight, yeah, and people have noticed, but it’s not because I’m afraid of gaining weight or worried about getting fat. If anything, I just have no appetite. I don’t feel hungry. Even when I do, I can’t summon the energy to cook or eat. My self-worth? Right now, I feel like a failure, but not because of my weight—I don’t even think about that much. It’s because I can’t seem to get out of this fog, and I don’t want to keep letting everyone down. I just feel… empty.

I’ve just turned 74, and since my husband passed four years ago, things have slowly changed. I live alone now, and to be honest, cooking for one doesn’t feel worth the effort. I often skip breakfast—sometimes lunch too—if I’m not hungry. My daughter says I look thin, and I suppose I have lost a bit of weight, though I haven’t stepped on the scale in months. I don’t *mean* to lose weight, but when I see things like butter, cheese, or even bread, I hesitate. There’s this nagging worry that eating them might… I don’t know, tip the balance somehow. I don’t fear becoming fat the way you see on TV, but I just feel safer keeping things light.  

Lately, I’ve been tired more than usual. I don’t get dressed until noon most days, and I’ve lost interest in the garden, which used to bring me such joy. I sleep, but not well. I wake early and just lie there. I wouldn’t say I’m sad all the time, but more like… empty. I don’t cry, but I don’t smile much either. I know I should eat more, but the thought of a heavy meal makes me uneasy. I just don’t feel like myself anymore—but I can’t say exactly why.

I won’t lie—I’ve been sad, tired, not sleeping well, and I don’t enjoy things like I used to. But it’s not just depression, I think. Even when I feel okay emotionally, I still can’t bring myself to eat. I watch the number on the scale go down and part of me worries, but another part feels relieved—like I’ve avoided something dangerous. The fear of gaining weight… it’s always there, like a voice warning me. I restrict food not because I lack appetite from sadness, but because I’m terrified of what it’ll do to my body.

Not because I’m not hungry, but because the thought of a full meal, especially anything rich or fatty—like butter on bread or a piece of meat—makes me anxious. I know I’ve lost weight; my clothes hang loose, and the cold bites through now. But I can’t bring myself to eat. I see my reflection and still feel like I might start gaining if I let go, even a little.

I’ll admit, I’ve been down—tired, withdrawn, not finding joy in things like repairing the lens or watching the storms roll in. But it’s not just sadness. It’s like my mind fixates on food and weight. I measure everything, even the peanut butter I used to spread thinly on crackers. My sister called the clinic, worried. But I tell you, I’m not *that* thin. I’m careful—that’s all. I can manage myself. I know what I’m doing. I don't need to gain weight. I *can’t*.
D021-D013_h022.question_b:
I’ve been working here at the lighthouse for twelve years now, and it used to be enough—just me, the sea, the quiet. But lately, I can't seem to muster the energy to do even the basics. For the past five months, everything feels heavy. I don’t sleep well, wake up exhausted, and some days I just sit in the keeper’s chair staring out at the rocks. I’ve lost interest in cooking—used to make decent meals, at least—now I often skip them altogether. Breakfast is usually nothing, and if I don’t feel like walking to the kitchen for dinner, I don’t. 

Weight’s dropped off me, I know—I can see it in the mirror—but I’m not scared of gaining it back. Honestly, I barely care how I look. I’m just… numb. My hands shake sometimes, and the station physician mentioned I’m too thin, but I told him it’s not worth worrying over. It’s not like I’m afraid of food. I just don’t feel like eating. Nothing tastes right. Nothing feels right. I don’t even care about the old comforts anymore—coffee, pie, doesn’t matter. It’s like the light keeps turning, but I’ve stopped seeing it.
